newsitem.title: UK: Inchcape shares gain on disposal news.
newsitem.headline: Inchcape shares gain on disposal news.

text.p: Shares in motor and distribution group Inchcape pushed higher on Tuesday after it said it would sell its insurance broking unit, Bain Hogg, to U.S. group Aon Corp, analysts said.

The move, which signals another step in plans to focus on the group's core activities of motor import and distribution, electronic marketing and soft drink bottling, comes just a week after news of the sale of its testing services division.
Shares in Inchcape were trading 5p higher at 285p shortly after the start of trading.
Bain Hogg is being sold for 160 million stg cash. Inchcape also said it expected an exceptional loss of about 195 million stg related to the sale.

"It's certainly been expected for them to get rid of Bain Hogg. The price is slightly disappointing and another 20 million pounds (stg) would have been nice but it is good they've bitten the bullet and are now focused and at these levels the shares look quite cheap," said one analyst.
The company said it had previously believed that a demerger was the most likely route for the divestment of Bain Hogg.

"However, having secured a price significantly above the value we expect the market to place on the company if demerged, I am convinced that today's disposal to Aon represents the best value for our shareholders," it said in a statement.
Inchcape said it planned to use proceeds from the sale to reduce its borrowings.

Taking into account the sale of Inchcape Testing Services last week and Bain Hogg, the company said its pro-forma gearing would have been about five percent based on its June 30 balance sheet compared to the reported 74 percent.
